pages.title: Port your number
pages.subtitle: Bring the number your customers already know — texting and calling.

blocks.note: Your current provider controls most of that timeline.

blocks.heading: Porting or hosting — pick the right one
blocks.intro: Two ways to bring a number into Salesmessage. Keeping your phone system and adding texting? Choose hosting. Want Salesmessage handling calls too? Choose porting.
blocks.footnote: Not sure where to start? Ask your Onboarding Manager or Customer Success Manager — we'll tell you which path fits.

blocks.title: Keep your current service active
blocks.text: Don't cancel with your current provider until the port is fully complete. Cancelling early is the most common cause of delays.

pages.title: What you need
pages.subtitle: Having everything ready before you submit keeps the port moving.

blocks.intro: Anything missing or mismatched sends the request back to the start.

rows.definition: Every number you want to move — local, toll-free, VoIP and landline all work.
Account number and PIN from your current provider. No PIN? Use the last four of the SSN.
Company name (business) or first and last name (personal), plus the full service address.
Letter of Authorization, signed and returned as a PDF to authorize the port request.
A bill from the last 30 days showing the number, or a screenshot from your provider.

blocks.title: Match your provider's records
blocks.text: A shortened business name or an old address is enough to get the port rejected. Check every detail before you submit.

pages.title: How to port
pages.subtitle: Five steps to follow, plus special cases to know about.

rows.definition: Collect your account details, the signed LOA and your proof of ownership.
Local U.S. numbers need A2P 10DLC approval in your Salesmessage account, or texts get filtered.
Don't cancel your current service — a disconnected number can't be ported.
Send everything via the porting request form, live chat or support@salesmessage.com.
If carriers request a correction, a same-day reply from you can save a week.
One number per port request only. We'll process multiples separately.
Unlock in settings first. Keep active throughout the port.
Separate, faster path — about 3-5 business days.
Not recommended — your phone loses its number during setup. Ask about alternatives.

blocks.title: What happens behind the scenes
blocks.text: Salesmessage is the winning carrier and your current provider the losing carrier. Once you send your details, we drive the request and keep you posted.

pages.title: After the port —
pages.subtitle: What changes once your number arrives in Salesmessage.

rows.definition: Doesn't come with it. Only new messages and calls appear in Salesmessage.
May need up to 3 business days for 10DLC sync. Error 30034 resolves itself.
Must be verified in Salesmessage before sending texts.
Doesn't transfer. Once your Salesmessage account is approved, additional local numbers are covered.

items.question: Does it cost anything to port a number in?
items.answer: No fee to port. Additional lines are $5 per month each.

items.question: Will we lose service during the port?
items.answer: No. Your number stays with your current provider until the port completes.

items.question: What if we want to port out later?
items.answer: Your new provider starts the request. Keep your subscription active and ask us for your CSR.
